recommendations.pathway_step: Referral arrival → first visit → treatment decision → first treatment (THL 21/2016 time points)
recommendations.problem: Goal 3's own wording, 'Potilaat pääsevät hoitoon tavoiteaikojen puitteissa' (S p.5), cannot be checked for any county: THL 2017 says national follow-up of cancer patients' access to care 'has been missing', and we found no later public regional series. The only public lung timing is a diagnosis clock for surgical patients in 5 collaborative areas, 2018–mid-2022.
recommendations.action: Week 1: the county extracts referral arrival, first visit, queue date and first treatment for every lung cancer of the last 12 months. That gives the county's own baseline in days 1–30. From week 5 the dates feed the Tasan dashboard weekly. If there is no treatment decision 28 days after referral arrival, an alert goes to the named nurse navigator. The navigator removes the blocker (test booking, result chasing, MDT slot, HUS/OYS slot) and is the single contact for patient and GP. A monthly board view shows % within 42 days, the median per step, and waits for non-pathway patients (to detect crowding out). The clock tells each county whether its problem is speed (→ T1) or who reaches curative treatment (→ T2). DATA-QUALITY TASK (days 1–30): before any baseline is published, check registry completeness against the EHR. In the 2024 report the age-standardised drug-therapy share is implausibly low in Varsinais-Suomi (0.8% men / 1.0% women), Vantaa-Kerava (3.7% / 3.8%) and Keski-Uusimaa (3.5% / 7.3%) vs ~25% nationally. Lapland is also low (10.0% / 15.3%; CIs below the national level). The likely cause is HILMO coding gaps (data team's inference). So the pilot checks drug, curative-RT and MDT codes, and the no-record cases, against the hospital's own records.
recommendations.already_exists: Hospitals hold the dates, and some have coordinators: roadmap 1.2.3 is still at 'survey existing models' (R p.32). What does not exist is a public, comparable, county-level clock for the Goal 3 target. Tasan is that missing public clock, not the first navigator in Finland.

recommendations.title: Close the missing step in Kymenlaakso's lung pathway: week-1 pathway map, then 3-day CT, reflex biomarkers and pre-agreed HUS surgery slots where missing
recommendations.pathway_step: Suspected lung cancer referral → CT/bronchoscopy/biopsy → biomarkers → lung meeting → HUS surgery decision → first treatment
recommendations.problem: Kymenlaakso diagnosed 591 lung cancers in 2019–2023, about 118 a year (csv denominator). Its surgical patients depend on another organisation: the surgery decision and the operation are made at HUS Meilahti in Helsinki (kymenhva.fi). Each hand-off between the Kotka pathway and HUS is a point where days can be lost. The county sits in Etelä-Suomi, the collaborative area with the longest median diagnosis→surgery time (46.0 d). That figure is fragile (see data basis) and is area-level context only, not a Kymenlaakso number. Kymenlaakso's crude curative-record share is 19.3% (CI 16.3–22.7) vs 27.0% nationally. Age-standardised (chart-digitised): men ≈18.0% (14.1–22.8), women ≈22.7% (17.2–29.3). South Karelia is similar (18.9% crude) but smaller.
recommendations.action: Week 1: map the current pathway (CT → bronchoscopy/EBUS/biopsy → pathology → biomarkers → Kymenhva lung meeting → HUS Meilahti surgery decision) using T3's dates. Then close only the step(s) that the map shows are missing, from a fixed menu: CT within 3 working days of referral; one diagnostic day; a reflex biomarker panel ordered by pathology for non-squamous NSCLC; surgical cases sent to HUS within 7 days of the lung meeting, into pre-agreed slots; T3's navigator owns the clock.
recommendations.already_exists: Kymenhva already runs a lung outpatient work-up and a multidisciplinary lung meeting (kymenhva.fi). T1 does not invent a pathway: it closes the missing step that the week-1 map finds.

recommendations.title: Every new Lapland lung cancer reviewed by the existing OYS lung-cancer MDT (by video), plus shared access to curative radiotherapy at OYS (RT referral, travel and accommodation, SBRT/chemoradiation slots)
recommendations.problem: HERO NUMBER (age-standardised, chart-digitised, ±1 pp): curative-treatment share in Lapland ≈16.2% for men (95% CI 12.7–20.4) vs ≈29.8% in Vantaa-Kerava (24.2–36.1); women ≈23.1% (17.9–29.0) vs ≈39.7% (33.1–47.0). The CIs do not overlap in either sex, so age structure does not explain the gap (crude: 18.5% vs 35.6%). Age-standardised SURGERY share for men is the same: Lapland 9.1% (6.0–13.7) vs Vantaa-Kerava 9.0% (5.5–14.1) (2024 report, Taulukko 3.7). So for men the gap is likely in curative radiotherapy. That is the data team's inference: the 2024 report does not separate curative from palliative RT. For women the surgery share also differs (10.4% vs 20.5%). Lapland's radiotherapy is given at OYS in Oulu (lapha.fi), hundreds of kilometres from much of Lapland. Distance worsens outcomes (roadmap p.12–13), and Norwegian data link travel to lower treatment odds.
recommendations.action: Two parts. (1) Review: week-1 audit of which 2025 Lapland lung cancers were discussed at the existing OYS lung-cancer MDT (answers mentor Q4). Then a rule that every new Lapland lung cancer is listed before the treatment-intent decision, with Lapland's clinician on video and ECOG/G8/CFS attached. (2) Curative-RT access (design arm, unpriced; see design): a direct MDT→OYS radiotherapy referral for curative SBRT or chemoradiation, with a reserved weekly slot quota for Lapland patients. Travel (Kela) and patient-hotel accommodation are booked by T3's navigator at the same time, and the decision is not left to the patient alone. Local follow-up is in Rovaniemi.
recommendations.already_exists: Yes. OYS states that the university hospital is responsible for lung-cancer MDTs, surgery and radiotherapy (oys.fi), and Lapland's radiotherapy is given at OYS (lapha.fi). T2 does not create a board: it closes coverage of the existing one to 100% of new Lapland cases, and turns a curative-RT recommendation into a booked slot with travel and accommodation arranged. The registry's 3.0% 'MDT recorded' figure for Lapland is NOT used as proof of a gap: Helsinki shows 0.1%, so it is a recording artefact.

recommendations.title: Regional suspected-cancer referral pathway (pakkeforløb-style) for 3–5 common cancers
recommendations.pathway_step: GP referral → specialist acceptance → first diagnostic visit
recommendations.problem: Finland has no cancer-specific pathway times in force. The only reference is THL Ohjaus 21/2016 (6 weeks referral→treatment), which is marked outdated and has no lung-specific limit. Cancer-specific times are due 2026–2028 (ROAD 3.1.2, p.57).
recommendations.action: The county adopts written referral criteria plus a 'syöpäepäily' (suspected cancer) referral flag for lung, colorectal, breast, prostate and one poor-prognosis cancer. The receiving unit books the first diagnostic step within a fixed number of days. Timestamps follow THL 21/2016.
recommendations.cost_estimate: ESTIMATE: mostly staff time (working groups, GP training). National funding is earmarked for pathways: €5 M/yr covering 2.5.2 and 3.1.2 (ROAD p.55).

recommendations.title: Named cancer-pathway coordinator (nurse navigator) from referral to first treatment
recommendations.pathway_step: Referral receipt → tests → MDT → treatment start
recommendations.problem: The roadmap notes that if the patient cannot demand urgent care or coordination is poor, total time 'may become very long' (ROAD p.13).
recommendations.action: Appoint 1–2 nurse coordinators at the central hospital. They own every flagged suspected-cancer referral: booking tests, chasing results, one phone number for patient and GP, and escalating breaches of the 6-week target.
recommendations.cost_estimate: 1 FTE nurse ≈ €46,902–€59,816/yr (sairaanhoitaja task-based €3,174 to total €4,048 per month, KT Oct 2025, × 12 × 1.2314 employer contributions, KT 2026) → 2 FTE ≈ €93,804–€119,632/yr.
recommendations.expected_effect: Norway introduced a cancer pathway coordinator role with its pathways. US navigation trial: OR 2.12 for timely diagnostic resolution at 365 days, with no difference at 60/180 days. The effect on Finnish waiting times is unverified.

recommendations.problem: Rejected or incomplete referrals and unclear cases add loops. Distances in Finland are long (>400 km to a central hospital for some, ROAD p.13).
recommendations.action: Specialists in key tumour areas answer GP e-consults within 2 working days, converting to a pathway referral when needed.
recommendations.cost_estimate: ESTIMATE: specialist time ~ a few hours/week per specialty (not costed). Reuses existing EHR messaging; vendor cost unknown.

recommendations.title: Pathologist-initiated reflex biomarker testing for NSCLC (and other agreed tumours)
recommendations.pathway_step: Histology → molecular result → first systemic treatment
recommendations.problem: Roadmap: molecular tests are done in many labs, answers are not ready fast enough for treatment planning, and there are notable regional differences (ROAD p.88).
recommendations.action: Pathology automatically orders the agreed biomarker panel at diagnosis of non-squamous NSCLC, without waiting for an oncologist request. Results go via electronic channels.
recommendations.cost_estimate: ESTIMATE: no extra tests per eligible patient (testing moves earlier). Some extra tests may follow in patients who would not have been tested. Panel price from the lab contract (not verified). National: roadmap 4.3.3 €400,000 (ROAD p.88).

recommendations.title: Fixed weekly MDT slots with pre-reserved treatment-start capacity

recommendations.problem: Norway found the decision→treatment interval to be the main delay. THL issued 2025 guidance on cancer MDT meetings (THL21 annex 2).

recommendations.action: Use remote oncology visits and give oral therapy and follow-up in the nearest hospital or health centre where clinically safe. Arrange patient travel at the time of the MDT.
recommendations.cost_estimate: ESTIMATE: offset partly by lower travel reimbursement (not quantified).
